title: 6-year-old student slapped over homework, dies after collapsing in teacher's lap
content: A six-year-old boy collapsed and died in a classroom at a private school. His family alleges a teacher beat him for not completing his homework assignment. The incident, captured on video, shows the teacher admonishing and slapping the student. The boy was declared dead after being brought to KG Hospital. Police and officials are investigating the circumstances surrounding the tragic death.

title: H-1B visa reality for Indians: Unpredictable costs, tougher odds & greater risks
content: H-1B visas have long been the main road for Indian professionals who are seeking employment, long-term career opportunities, and eventually even the green card in the US. But over the past two years, several changes in the H-1B visa application and selection criterion have added a huge layer of uncertainty.

title: No bachelors, no biryani, no dogs: What your RWA can legally ban, and what it can’t
content: Resident welfare associations possess limited powers governed by law and their own documents.  RWAs can manage common areas and enforce valid bye-laws for community well-being.  However, associations cannot override individual legal or proprietary rights of residents.  Rules must have a proper basis and be applied fairly to all members.  Disputes often arise from unclear rules and the need for greater transparency.

title: Amit Shah hails South's development in CMs meet, cites 3 pillars of progress

He said that "the whole of India should learn from South India in these two areas," as per the home ministery's statement.

title: How an ex-Buddhist monk & Meta engineer founded a startup that now rivals Accenture
content: Lilly Chen, a former Buddhist monk and Meta software engineer, founded Contenda after a hackathon.  She and three friends turned a pandemic-era project into a successful startup.  The company focuses on helping businesses repurpose technical content effectively.  Contenda secured one million dollars in pre-seed funding in March 2021.  Chen now leads the company as its chief executive officer.

title: Why UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi' matters more than ever in 2027 assembly election

Parties are actively wooing women with welfare schemes and cash transfers.  Both the BJP and Samajwadi Party are making substantial promises to female voters.  Winning the trust of over six crore women voters will be crucial for electoral success.

title: Meet 10-yr-old Hsu Ting-wei, winner of Silicon Valley invention award
content: At the Silicon Valley International Festival, Taiwanese innovators caught the global spotlight with remarkable inventions. A ten-year-old prodigy took home a prestigious award for crafting an AI-driven electronic nose capable of detecting hazardous substances and potentially stopping disease outbreaks. This year, Taiwanese competitors celebrated a landmark achievement, claiming twenty-four gold medals and numerous honors, showcasing their ingenuity and practical solutions that captivated both judges and audiences.

title: NASA launches $500,000 challenge to improve space weather predictions
content: In an effort to enhance the understanding of upper atmospheric conditions, NASA is inviting proposals for affordable technology solutions. The Orbital Clarity Challenge aims to refine predictions regarding satellite orbit variations caused by atmospheric drag. Participants stand to win up to $500,000 for their innovative concepts, along with the opportunity for a free test flight to test their technologies.

title: Steam tug that survived two world wars reappears in Serbia after drought
content: Amidst severe drought, a historic steam tug once lost beneath the Sava River has resurfaced, delighting locals who flock to witness 'Sava's Titanic'. This vessel, which sank in 1945 after a tragic encounter with a mine, revitalizes memories of the Balkans' complex history. Its emergence underscores the grim water shortages plaguing significant European rivers today.

title: Anthropic's AI designed proteins in 2 days, a job that takes scientists months
content: Anthropic says Claude designed protein binders that worked against 14 of 15 targets, with Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience validating 354 binders from 1,320 designs. Hit rates reached 35.1%, well above the field's usual 10-15%. A separate test saw Claude Opus 5 match a contract lab's purity reading in 19 minutes. title: BNP's Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected 23rd president of Bangladesh

The voting took place between 2 pm and 5 pm local time under the supervision of chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin.

title: Chandigarh was built as a planned city. So why does it keep sinking in the rain?

title: Centre gives nod to set up a bench of J&K HC in Ladakh
content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday decided to set up a bench of high court of Jammu and Kashmir in Ladakh. In a post on X, Union home minister Amit Shah said the government is "fully committed" to the all-round development of Ladakh and claimed that the decision will enhance access to justice to citizens living in remote areas. "The Union cabinet, under the leadership of the PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji, has decided to set up a bench of the high court of Jammu and Kashmir in Ladakh," Shah said. "This will significantly enhance access to justice for citizens living in remote areas of Ladakh by reducing the time required to avail themselves of the legal services they are entitled to. The Govt is fully committed to the all-round development of Ladakh and to ensuring constitutional safeguards," he added.

End of Article
